applied.quote: [Interpreted] Conclusion. At the resolution these data permit, Ghanaian P. falciparum shows very low but statistically detectable differentiation at the retained common variants. Five of the six pairwise estimates have 95% confidence intervals excluding zero; only Guinea savanna against the transitional zone, where n = 25, spans it. Very low is not the same as undetectable, and neither is a demonstration of random mating, for which these data contain no direct evidence. What the sensitivity analysis adds is stability of the magnitude rather than absence of the effect: the maximum pairwise FST stays within 0.00204-0.00255 across all six threshold scenarios, over 1,900 to 4,403 isolates and 3,275 to 10,876 SNPs, so the headline result is insensitive to both of the cuts that define the dataset. The companion claim does not survive the same treatment. The region-level isolation-by-distance result is significant at the published thresholds and at MAF >= 0.02, but in only 2 of 6 threshold scenarios and 4 of 7 leave-one-region-out replicates, and this report therefore no longer asserts a distance effect, weak or otherwise. What remains of the spatial signal is a single south-to-north contrast, visible in the FST ranking and in the K = 2 minor component, with no robust evidence that genetic distance scales with geographic distance. That very low differentiation is a statement about neutral common-variant structure only: neutral common-variant differentiation between zones is negligible, so a spatially sparse design is adequate for characterising neutral structure, but marker-frequency representativeness is a separate question, and the resistance panel in this analysis shows significant between-zone variation at p < 0.001 at pfdhfr, pfdhps and pfaat1. That threshold is stated because it is a selection: on the four-zone chi-square as reported, several further loci are nominally significant at p < 0.05, among them pfcrt I356T (p = 1.6 x 10 to the -3), pfmdr2 I492V (p = 0.020) and pfmdr1 N86Y (p = 0.029). Low neutral FST therefore does not license an assumption that marker frequencies are spatially representative. The pfk13 result is a genuine tested negative - no screened resistance allele occurs at any of the 23 codons, which cover the complete WHO-validated set of 14 and all 6 candidates: twenty-two are fixed at the reference residue and codon 458 is at 0.9995 on a single Asn458Asp call, which is not the validated N458Y, on 1,845 to 1,876 isolates called per codon - rather than an untested absence; it is also a statement about 2009-2021 and not about current parasite populations. The XtX set remains a ranked candidate list, of which 13 SNPs survive FDR 10% and two adjacent chromosome-11 sites - one of them the fifth-ranked SNP overall - are flagged lower confidence on ExcessHet and InbreedingCoeff grounds. All zone-level results describe a compound variable in which ecology, administrative region, collection period and sequencing study cannot be separated; that is a property of the Pf8 metadata, not of the analysis.

applied.quote: [Interpreted] Robustness of these conclusions to the corrected re-runs and the final checks. The population-structure readings held on a 16.6% larger SNP panel (3,359 to 3,916 SNPs) with corrected filter ordering, a bitwise-reproducible single-threaded BayPass, seeded permutation tests and full false-discovery accounting: near-panmixia, maximum FST of approximately 0.0023, and a near-flat ADMIXTURE cross-validation curve. Three quantities moved and should not be described as unchanged: the XtX threshold (the manuscript's 8-thread run gave 11.232, the final single-threaded run gives 10.840), the outlier count (15 to 19) and the outlier gene list (11 to 13 genes). One conclusion has since been lost, and it was the report's only positive spatial finding. The threshold sensitivity analysis shows the region-level Mantel result significant in 2 of 6 scenarios, and it also withdraws the earlier claim that the result no longer depends on the censoring of negative FST pairs: of the six scenarios only the baseline clears p < 0.05 both censored and uncensored, the second significant scenario (MAF >= 0.02) giving p = 0.047 censored against p = 0.050 uncensored. Isolation by distance is retained in the report and reported with the scenarios in which it fails, but it is graded not robust, and the previous version's listing of it among the strengthened results is withdrawn. Two strengthenings stand. Near-panmixia is now supported by FST stability across 0.00204-0.00255 over all six scenarios, which is better evidence than any single run could give; and TreeMix now carries jackknife edge standard errors, so the m = 2 graph is reported as a selected descriptive model rather than as a settled edge count. Two further checks changed nothing material. Re-running the three ordinations on the 1,900-isolate analysis set rather than the 4,905 pre-QC isolates leaves the reading intact - silhouette by zone -0.020 against -0.016 on the full set, so removing polyclonal and clonally redundant isolates does not sharpen the structure; trustworthiness 0.499 (UMAP), 0.526 (t-SNE), 0.510 (PCoA), PCoA distance correlation 0.287 against 0.322 - and the call-quality audit clears the outlier set while downgrading two chromosome-11 SNPs. The resistance panel is a different matter and was not confirmed but replaced: an external critique upheld in full showed that the marker identification method was unsound, and the panel was rebuilt from the codon up, changing the pfdhfr triple-mutant figure, adding a locus that had been missing altogether, correcting a residue call, correcting the pfk13 list, and replacing the validation argument. The population analyses are therefore a partial confirmation with two strengthened results, one lost result, two downgraded outlier SNPs and one materially revised candidate list; the resistance results are new.

applied.quote: [Interpreted] A fifth round, and the loss of a result. Four outstanding robustness checks were run at final revision, and they are the reason this version grades one finding lower than the last. Three of the four left the conclusions standing or strengthened them: the maximum pairwise FST varies only between 0.00204 and 0.00255 across six threshold scenarios spanning 1,900 to 4,403 isolates and 3,275 to 10,876 SNPs, so near-panmixia does not depend on the Fws or MAF cuts; the 19 XtX outliers are better-supported calls than the rest of the scanned panel rather than artefacts, although two adjacent chromosome-11 sites are downgraded within that set; and re-running the ordinations on the 1,900-isolate analysis set, so that they describe the same isolates as everything else, changes nothing material. The fourth check overturned a conclusion. The region-level isolation-by-distance result - the only positive spatial finding in this report - is significant in 2 of those 6 threshold scenarios and in 4 of 7 leave-one-region-out replicates, collapsing when Upper East is dropped, and is therefore graded not robust wherever it appears below. It is not deleted: it holds at the published thresholds, and it is reported together with the scenarios in which it fails. But it can no longer be described as supported, moderately supported, or a weak but real distance effect, and the preceding version's listing of it among the strengthened results is withdrawn. The remaining check, the provenance of the agro-ecological zone layer, cannot be closed analytically at all and stays open.

Maximum pairwise FST is 0.00232 (SE 0.00053) against 0.0024 before; the ADMIXTURE cross-validation curve is still near-flat, with K = 2 at 0.83925 against K = 1 at 0.84384; and near-panmixia across Ghana's agro-ecological zones still holds. A headline that survives a materially larger panel and a stricter multiplicity correction is better supported than one that was merely never tested. Two limits on that reassurance should be stated with it. It applies to the population-structure results, which the marker-panel rebuilds do not touch; and it is an internal-consistency argument of exactly the kind that the pattern above shows to be insufficient on its own.

applied.quote: Isolation by distance is withdrawn as a supported result. Two checks now bear on this test, they vary different things, and they agree. The leave-one-region-out jackknife (Table 6.7) finds it significant in 4 of 7 replicates, with significance collapsing whenever the region defining either end of the distance range is dropped — Upper East at the long end, Greater Accra or Eastern at the short end. The threshold sensitivity (Table 6.7a) finds it significant in 2 of 6 scenarios, and the relaxation that most directly tests the filter doing the most work — removing the Fws cut, which more than doubles the isolate count to 4,403 — moves p from 0.0252 to 0.1792. The honest statement is that the isolation-by-distance result holds at the published thresholds and almost nowhere else. The original manuscript's "weak but detectable" distance effect, retained through every earlier revision of this section including the one that reported the jackknife improving from 2 of 7 to 4 of 7, cannot be retained now, and the grading of this result in Sections 1, 7 and 10 as supported or moderately supported must change with it. This is the only positive spatial finding in the analysis and it is the one that did not survive the two checks the audit identified as most needed. It is reported here in full rather than deleted — the point estimate at the published thresholds is unchanged and a reader is entitled to it — but it should not be cited as evidence of distance-limited gene flow in Ghana.

applied.quote: [Interpreted] The evidence for negligible differentiation is strong, but it is neither five independent lines nor a test of random mating. FST, ADMIXTURE and TreeMix are three summaries of one genotype matrix: all three are computed from the same per-zone allele counts, and at this level of differentiation a four-population covariance matrix and the pairwise FST matrix are near-deterministic functions of each other. Only the ordinations use a different input — MalariaGEN's published Pf8 genotype-distance matrix — and they are now computed on the same 1,900 isolates as everything else, because stage 3 has been re-run on the analysis set (silhouette by zone −0.020; Table 8.2 row 21, Figure 8.1). The agreement between rows 1, 3 and 4 of Table 7.1 is therefore substantially arithmetic, not corroborative. What this revision adds is robustness rather than independence: the FST summary has been recomputed under six combinations of the two thresholds that define the dataset, and the maximum pairwise value moves only between 0.00204 and 0.00255 (row 5 of Table 7.1; Table 8.3). Those six scenarios are not independent lines either — they are the same pipeline on overlapping data — but they establish that the headline does not depend on the analyst's threshold choices, which is a different and more useful thing. The region-level Mantel test does not share that robustness, and it has to be given up. It is a fourth summary of the same matrix, computed from region-level FST, so it was never independent of the others; and it is significant in only 2 of 6 threshold scenarios and 4 of 7 leave-one-region-out replicates, so it cannot be cited as a converging line at all (Table 7.2, row 1). It was the one result here carrying a positive structure claim, and losing it is a real loss rather than a tidying-up. Described accurately, what remains is: three summaries of one 3,916-SNP genotype matrix (ADMIXTURE on 3,385 LD-pruned sites of it), plus three ordinations of an independently published distance matrix on the same 1,900 isolates, all pointing the same way, and insensitive to both thresholds that define the dataset. The negative half of the result is better supported than it was. The positive half is gone.

applied.quote: [Interpreted] Ghanaian P. falciparum behaves as a single, largely panmictic population for common neutral variation, with weak departures detectable in minor-component ancestry and in resistance-marker frequencies. A region-level distance effect is present at the published thresholds but disappears under almost any variation of them, so it is not among the departures this analysis can claim. Those departures that remain are not a clean latitudinal ordering — the transitional zone breaks the monotone pattern in most variables examined (§7.2), pfaat1 S258L excepted — but they are not nothing either. This is a substantive answer to the thesis's first objective, and a negative one for the strong form of its hypothesis: the ecological zones are not acting as demographic barriers at a scale these data can detect. It is not, however, a negative answer for the thesis's third objective; see §7.4 and §7.5.

applied.quote: [Interpreted] That the headline is a negative is not surprising, and that is a point in its favour. Ghana is approximately 670 km north to south, human mobility along the north–south corridor is substantial, P. falciparum undergoes obligate sexual recombination in the mosquito, and transmission across most of the country is high. All four favour genetic homogenisation. The finding is consistent with the continental picture, in which West African parasite populations form a single major subpopulation (Amambua-Ngwa et al., 2019), and with the observation that differentiation within West African countries is weak relative to the differentiation between endemicity strata that Mobegi et al. (2014) reported between The Gambia and Guinea.

applied.quote: [Interpreted] What the neutral result licenses. Neutral common-variant differentiation between zones is negligible — maximum pairwise FST 0.00232, with one of six confidence intervals spanning zero (Guinea savanna vs transitional zone, [−0.00083, 0.00178]), and the maximum staying within 0.00204–0.00255 across six threshold scenarios (Table 8.3) — so a spatially sparse design is adequate for characterising neutral structure. Marker-frequency representativeness is a separate question, and the rebuilt resistance panel shows significant between-zone variation at six of the nine panel genes, including pfdhfr, pfdhps and pfaat1 (the others being pfcrt, pfmdr1 and pfmdr2). If the question is whether a handful of sites will give a representative picture of the neutral genomic background, these data answer yes; if the question is whether those sites will give a representative picture of resistance-marker frequencies, these data answer no.

applied.quote: [Observed] The resistance panel settles the question empirically, and the answer is no. Marker frequencies do differ by zone. pfaat1 S258L spans about 28 percentage points from coast to far north (0.824 to 0.544, χ² p = 1.89 × 10⁻¹⁸, n = 1,896 called). pfdhps G437 — the allele that was missing from the panel altogether in the previous draft — runs 0.964 in deciduous forest and 0.941 on the coast against 0.875 in Guinea savanna and 0.800 in the transitional zone (χ² p = 1.2 × 10⁻⁶, n = 1,892). The pfdhfr codons are heterogeneous across the four zones (S108N χ² p = 9.4 × 10⁻⁷; C59R 4.8 × 10⁻⁵; N51I 2.4 × 10⁻⁴) and the IRN triple-mutant haplotype itself runs 0.750 in Guinea savanna, 0.788 in deciduous forest, 0.867 on the coast and 0.880 in the transitional zone on 25 isolates. These are all four-zone heterogeneity tests; no directional south-versus-Guinea contrast was run, and the transitional zone's values rest on 25 isolates (§7.2). A sentinel site on the coast and a sentinel site in Upper East would report materially different resistance-marker profiles from the same panmictic parasite population. The operational implication is the reverse of the previous draft's: neutral structure can be characterised sparsely; marker frequencies cannot. A surveillance design intended to track resistance needs to span the gradient, and this analysis is evidence for rather than against that requirement.

The marker panel is a different matter: it was not re-run but rebuilt, by a new script that reconstructs codons rather than matching annotation strings, and several of its conclusions did change (§7.5, §8). applied.quote: [Interpreted] The containment corollary, correctly scoped. Because no neutral barrier is detectable at the retained common variants, this analysis supplies no evidence of a barrier for a geographically targeted containment intervention to exploit. That is an absence of evidence at the resolution these data permit, not a demonstration that parasite exchange across Ghana is unobstructed: a low differentiation estimate does not measure connectivity, and the study, geography and year confounding is not removed by it. That remains a reasonable reading, and it is now the better supported for the absence of a robust distance effect: there is not even a weak isolation-by-distance gradient left to qualify it. It does not follow that spread will be uniform in rate or that a single site will see it first; the pfaat1, pfdhps and pfdhfr zone differences show that selection and drug pressure impose their own geography, which negligible neutral differentiation does not predict. Whether gene flow is in fact free is not measured here: a low differentiation estimate at retained common variants does not quantify contemporary connectivity.

applied.quote: [Calculated] The four outstanding checks have now been run. Three confirmed robustness; one overturned a conclusion. (i) Threshold sensitivity. scripts/step13_sensitivity.py rebuilds the analysis matrix under six combinations of the two thresholds that define the dataset — the Fws monoclonality cut, which discards 57 per cent of isolates and does so unevenly by zone, and the MAF floor, which discards 99.8 per cent of sites — and recomputes pairwise FST and the region-level Mantel test for each (Table 8.3). Near-panmixia is insensitive to both: maximum pairwise FST moves only between 0.00204 and 0.00255, a total spread of 0.0005, over sample sizes from 1,900 to 4,403 and SNP counts from 3,275 to 10,876. That stability is the best-evidenced result in the whole analysis — evidence that the measured differentiation does not depend on the threshold choices, not evidence about the processes that produced it. Isolation by distance is not: the Mantel test is significant in 2 of 6 scenarios, failing at every relaxation of the Fws cut and at MAF ≥ 0.01, and holding only at the published thresholds and marginally at MAF ≥ 0.02. Taken with the leave-one-region-out jackknife, which already showed 4 of 7 and collapse when Upper East is dropped, the finding must now be reported as not robust. It was the manuscript's only positive spatial finding, and it did not survive the two checks the audit itself identified as most needed. That is the overturned conclusion, and it is a loss rather than a refinement. (ii) Outlier variant quality. The 19 XtX outliers are better-supported calls than the rest of the panel, not worse, and the exported-protein artefact worry is closed; two adjacent chromosome-11 SNPs are downgraded for an unrelated and still-unverified reason (§7.2 and its note). (iii) Stage 3 re-run on the 1,900-isolate analysis set. The ordination conclusion is unchanged, the silhouette becomes slightly more negative, and the figures now describe the same sample as every other result (Figure 8.1). (iv) GeoJSON provenance remains open and cannot be closed analytically; it requires a written enquiry to the likely custodian (§9.3). Two secondary observations from (i) are worth recording in their own right: relaxing Fws slightly raises FST (0.00232 to 0.00255), so the polyclonal isolates the filter removes were not masking differentiation; and tripling the SNP count via MAF ≥ 0.01 lowers it (0.00204), as expected if rarer variants are less differentiated between zones.

applied.quote: [Calculated] Isolation by distance is no longer a supported result. This is the one population-genetic conclusion that the threshold sensitivity overturned, and the loss is a real one: it was the manuscript's only positive spatial finding. The numbers themselves are unchanged. At the published thresholds the region-level Mantel correlation is r = 0.4269 (p = 0.0252) with negative FST pairs floored to zero, and r = 0.4138 (p = 0.0413) without flooring; three of the 21 region pairs were affected, so on the final matrix the censoring no longer determines significance, although both versions are reported and the disclosure stands. What has changed is what those numbers are worth. The test is significant in two of the six threshold scenarios — the published one and MAF >= 0.02 at p = 0.0467 — and fails at every relaxation of the Fws cut (p = 0.0874, 0.1687 and 0.1792) and at MAF >= 0.01 (p = 0.0617). The two thresholds fail it in different ways and the difference is informative. Relaxing Fws changes the correlation itself, which falls from 0.4269 to 0.2447 as the isolate count rises from 1,900 to 4,403; relaxing MAF leaves the correlation essentially untouched (0.4325 at MAF >= 0.01, 0.4341 at MAF >= 0.02) and moves only the permutation p-value across the 0.05 line. So the result is sensitive to which isolates are analysed in a way that cannot be written off as lost power, and it is marginal at the published MAF floor in a way that a different floor is enough to disturb. Taken with the leave-one-region-out jackknife, which already found it significant in only four of seven replicates — significance lost on dropping Upper East (n = 1,334; r = +0.260, p = 0.218), Greater Accra (n = 204; r = +0.250, p = 0.232) or Eastern (n = 34; r = +0.288, p = 0.136) — the honest grade is not robust: it holds at the published thresholds on the complete set of seven regions, and almost nowhere else. At zone level it was never demonstrable at all: r = 0.4709 with p = 0.1218 over six pairs, none of the four leave-one-out replicates significant, and only 24 distinct permutations available, which is a resolution limit rather than a negative finding. The result is not deleted and should not be. A correlation of 0.43 over 21 region pairs that survives neither a change of monoclonality cut nor a change of MAF floor is a statement about this dataset's resolution, not evidence of a distance gradient in Ghanaian Plasmodium falciparum, and it is reported here with its sensitivity so that a successor with more populations or finer spatial units can test it properly. Not robust.

applied.quote: [Interpreted] What this implies for surveillance design, stated narrowly. Neutral common-variant differentiation between zones is negligible, so a spatially sparse design is adequate for characterising neutral structure. The withdrawal of the isolation-by-distance result reinforces that narrow claim rather than complicating it: on the present evidence there is no robust distance gradient for a denser neutral design to resolve either. Marker-frequency representativeness is a separate question, and it is the question sentinel surveillance actually answers; on that question this analysis finds significant between-zone variation at pfdhps 437 (p = 1.2 x 10-6), pfdhfr (p <= 2.43 x 10-4 at all three triple-mutant codons; the largest of the three is 2.425 x 10-4 at Asn51Ile) and pfaat1 (p = 1.9 x 10-18). The original Section 7.4 conclusion — that sentinel surveillance at a small number of sites is an adequate design for detecting emergence — is therefore withdrawn in its unqualified form, here and in Section 7.4. This is the clearest case in the manuscript of a conclusion that the resistance panel reverses, and the two sections must not disagree.

applied.quote: [Interpreted] A closing assessment. The analysis has done what a baseline characterisation should do: established the scale of structure, found it to be small, identified precisely which design features limit what can be inferred, and produced a short candidate list for follow-up. What has changed across the three rounds is the standing of the negative results, the standing of our own corrections, and now the standing of a positive result. The absence of resistance loci from the outlier scan was not a result at all but a filter artefact, and correcting it converted the thesis's third objective from a null finding into its best-supported positive one — pfdhps G437 at 0.897 and zone-structured, the pfdhfr triple mutant measured as a haplotype at 0.771, and pfaat1 S258L as a strong candidate whose demonstrated functional effect is modest and background-dependent. The absence of artemisinin resistance is now genuinely tested, across the complete WHO-validated and candidate sets, on 1,845 to 1,876 called isolates per codon over 2009–2021, and genuinely negative. But the first correction of the panel was itself wrong in four ways, and only an external reader caught it. The honest conclusion is therefore two claims rather than one. A negative result is worth nothing until the thing it denies has been shown to be measurable. And internal consistency is not correctness: every defect in the first corrected panel came from a list, a direction or a label taken on trust, and the verification architecture built to catch stale numbers was never built to ask whether the inputs were the right ones. The third round adds a third claim, and it is the least comfortable of the three. Four checks this list carried as outstanding were run, and the one previously described here as addressing "the two most likely reviewer objections" removed a finding instead of answering them: isolation by distance survives neither a relaxation of the monoclonality cut nor a lower MAF floor, and is significant at two of six threshold settings. The gain and the loss come from the same six runs. The check that destroyed the spatial finding is the check that made near-panmixia the best-evidenced conclusion in the manuscript, because FST moved by less than 0.0005 while the Mantel p-value crossed 0.05 four times. A result that holds only at the thresholds that produced it was never a result; it was a setting. The manuscript is shorter by one finding and better by one method, and the third claim is simply that: a threshold is a hypothesis, and until it has been varied, every conclusion downstream of it is conditional on a number nobody tested.

applied.quote: [Observed] This appendix exists for traceability, and it now records three rounds. Round one, 9–10 October 2026: an adversarial multi-agent audit. Eight reviewers working across separate dimensions raised 110 findings, each of which was then put to three independent verifiers prompted to refute it and defaulting to refuted where they could not substantiate the claim. A finding counts as confirmed only where at least two of three verifiers failed to refute it after checking the code, data or outputs themselves. Sixty-one findings were confirmed — 14 high severity, 31 medium, 16 low — with 19 disputed and 21 refuted. Thirty verifications in the reproducibility dimension were lost to a rate limit and are recorded as unverified rather than confirmed. Seven confirmed defects required code changes; stages 4 to 9 were re-run on 10 October 2026 with all seven in place. Round two, 10 October 2026: an external critique of the corrected manuscript. It raised five points. All five were upheld and four were defects in the analysis code, not in the prose — in the resistance panel that round one had introduced to fix its own largest finding. The panel was rebuilt as scripts/step12_codon_panel.py and every resistance number in this revision was read from that script's outputs. This is the fourth consecutive round in which a correction contained its own defect, and the pattern is consistent: each layer was checked for internal consistency against our own outputs, and what escaped was external correctness — whether the marker list matched an authoritative source, whether the annotation direction matched the reference genome, whether a co-occurrence claim had co-occurrence data behind it. The verification architecture was built to catch stale numbers, and it did. It was not built to ask whether the inputs were the right ones. Round three, 10 October 2026: the four outstanding robustness checks. This round was not an audit of the manuscript but the execution of four items that Section 10.4 carried as outstanding, and it is recorded here because one of them overturned a conclusion instead of confirming it. The Fws and MAF sensitivity analysis (scripts/step13_sensitivity.py) withdrew isolation by distance as a supported result — significant in two of six threshold scenarios — and, from the same six runs, made near-panmixia the best-evidenced conclusion in the manuscript. The outlier quality check cleared the exported-protein artefact concern and downgraded two chromosome-11 SNPs on an ExcessHet and InbreedingCoeff signal. Stage 3 was re-run on the analysis set. The GeoJSON provenance cannot be closed analytically and remains open. Round three found no defect in the prose and none in the analysis code; what it found was that a published result depended on the thresholds that produced it. Two integrity incidents occurred during the round and are registered as rows 13 and 14 of Table F.1 rather than left in the logs.
